sentiment.rationale: Forward guidance was materially reduced: full-year guidance was withdrawn, Q2 revenue is expected to decline 8-10%, and Q2 gross margins are expected to decline ~150 bps. Management explicitly stated 'a comeback at this scale takes time... we have yet to turn the corner' and cited elevated inventories, higher promotional activity, and underperformance in digital and China. These are structural headwinds, not one-time items, and the withdrawal of full-year guidance signals significant near-term uncertainty.

summary.revenue: $11.6 billion, down 10% on a reported basis and down 9% on a currency-neutral basis.
summary.eps: Diluted EPS of $0.70, down 26% from $0.94 in the prior year.
summary.guidance: Full-year guidance withdrawn; Q2 revenue expected to decline 8-10%; Q2 gross margins expected to decline approximately 150 bps; Q2 SG&A expected to be roughly flat; Q2 effective tax rate expected in the high-teens range.
summary.margin: Gross margin increased 120 bps to 45.4% in Q1; Q2 gross margin expected to decline approximately 150 bps.
key_risks: Elevated inventory requiring higher promotional activity and creating gross margin pressure.
Traffic declines across NIKE Direct and partner stores in Greater China were more significant than anticipated.
Classic footwear franchises (Air Force 1, Air Jordan 1, Dunk) declined nearly 50% on NIKE Digital and are expected to continue to be a headwind.
Spring '25 order books came in roughly flat versus prior year, a little lighter than planned.
Full-year guidance withdrawn and Investor Day postponed, increasing near-term business and strategy visibility uncertainty.
key_opportunities: New footwear products revenue up strong double-digits year over year, with franchises like Sabrina, Kobe, Alphafy, Vomero 5, V2K, and P-6000 scaling rapidly.
Men's and women's running footwear delivered positive growth in Q1, a meaningful improvement versus the prior quarter, with spring order books projecting double-digit growth.
Strong brand investment in the Paris Olympics campaign, with NIKE owning over 60% of total share of voice during the games.
Positive partner feedback on future product pipeline, with new concepts like women's fitness at DICK'S and Home Court at Foot Locker showing early success.

management_tone.label: cautious
management_tone.justification: Management repeatedly emphasized that 'a comeback at this scale takes time' and 'we have yet to turn the corner,' while withdrawing full-year guidance and flagging multiple headwinds.
